subject: Re: Boreal — data provenance, transit, and LLM adaptation terms
messages:
From: Alex Byrne <alex.byrne@borealhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: procurement@borealhealth.com
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Data provenance and transit — adaptation terms

Marcus,

Thanks for the demo earlier — Boreal's legal/procurement team asked me to follow up on a couple of guarantees we need in the DPA and the operational evidence we need before procurement signs off. High level asks:

- A clear commitment that Boreal customer interactions will not be used to adapt or update Redwood models (we call it a "model adaptation" ban).
- Ownership/entitlement language that confirms Boreal owns prompts and responses (or at minimum has exclusive rights to derivative outputs).
- A list of subprocessors and confirmation of EU residency for any data-processing subprocessors that will touch Boreal PII.

Can you send a redline of the DPA with the proposed language and any operational summary we can present to our InfoSec folks? We should be able to finalize procurement if we get: the signed DPA, subprocessor residency chart, and a short ops note describing retention and export controls.

Appreciate it — aim to close this week if possible.

Best,
Alex Byrne
Head of Cloud Procurement
Boreal Health

--
Attachment: Boreal_RFI_notes.xlsx (reference)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Byrne <alex.byrne@borealhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 12:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data provenance and transit — adaptation terms

Alex — thanks, great to hear the demo was useful.

We can cover all three asks; attached is a draft DPA amendment (PDF) that has a concise "no-model-adaptation" commitment (we used that term to avoid ambiguity) and explicit derivative-entitlement language: Redwood will not use customer content to update or fine-tune any production models that serve non-Boreal customers, and Boreal retains exclusive rights to customer-provided prompts and generated responses with the exceptions enumerated in section 4.2 (security/abuse detection).

Operational proof attached (ops-proof-no-adapt-summary.txt) — short bullets on how this is enforced:
- Ephemeral inference: per-session KV caches are isolated and garbage-collected after 24 hours unless explicitly persisted by the customer.
- Prefix caching: limited to acceleration contexts; keys are tenant-scoped and cannot be merged into training datasets.
- Telemetry isolation: token-level telemetry is routed to an onshore EU analytics cluster for Boreal; we can provide a scrubbed sample pipeline.
- Subprocessor gating: any subprocessor with access to plaintext PII is limited to EU-based regions for this workload.

Attached also is a CSV export of our subprocessor matrix with residence columns highlighted. A couple of notes for procurement/legal:
- We can add a short warranty clause about the residency of subprocessors for this contract's scope (EU-residency for PII processing).
- For extra assurance we support an audit right with a narrow scope (technical controls review in a mutually agreed window).

Next steps I suggest: you review the DPA redline, Kimberly (cc) will confirm the drafting tweaks for IP language, and if that's acceptable we'll circulate for countersignature via DocuSign.

Scheduling note: David and I are available for a 30-min call Monday to walk InfoSec through the ops bullets if helpful.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Account — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_amendment_2027-04-03.pdf; subprocessors_eu_residency_v2.csv; ops-proof-no-adapt-summary.txt

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Byrne <alex.byrne@borealhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Data provenance and transit — adaptation terms

Alex / Marcus — Quick drafting notes from legal:

1) Ownership and derivatives: instead of "exclusive rights" language, we propose a short, explicit clause that Boreal retains ownership of customer-provided input and exclusive rights to derivative outputs (textual responses and embeddings) for the term of the agreement, subject to limited exceptions (regulatory disclosure, abuse mitigation). This avoids ambiguous IP terms while giving Boreal the practical protections procurement wants.

2) "No-model-adaptation" scope: define what counts as "adaptation" — we suggest: (a) no incorporation of raw customer content into training corpora for production model updates; (b) allowed uses for narrow-scope on-prem sandboxing/feature engineering only with prior written consent. This avoids blocking feature experiments entirely.

3) Subprocessor residency warranty: we can add a warranty for EU residency for subprocessors that handle plaintext PII for the Boreal environment; however, we recommend a transitional carveout for legacy infra (we identify two transient partners in the CSV flagged as "migration in progress"). We'll document migration dates in an appendix.

Marcus — I redlined the DPA (attached in the draft). If Boreal agrees, legal can sign off and we'll route to DocuSign.

Kimberly Park
VP, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Byrne <alex.byrne@borealhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: procurement@borealhealth.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 15:04:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Data provenance and transit — adaptation terms

Thanks Marcus / Kimberly — this looks reasonable and maps to our procurement checklist. A few clarifying items before we click send:

- Can you confirm the two "migration in progress" subprocessors will be EU-resident by 2027-05-31? Procurement needs a target date.
- Can you provide a sanitized sample of the telemetry routing manifest (we only need headers/field names) for our InfoSec review — that will speed the internal signoff.

If those two items are green, we will countersign the DPA and route the DocuSign to you. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alex Byrne
Head of Cloud Procurement
Boreal Health
